procedure_signature.notes: Particle-versus-rigid-body modeling, the reciprocal of mechanics_model_selection signed immediately prior in the same subtopic. Three criteria authored — concurrency, question-dependence, rotational tendency — with the governing point that SIZE IS NOT THE CRITERION. DISTINGUISHING PAIR verified to bite: a 12 m radio mast is correctly modelled as a PARTICLE and a 40 mm bracket as a RIGID BODY, so size runs exactly opposite to the model choice across the pair and cannot be mistaken for the discriminator. Case 3 turns on the question alone — the same ladder with the same forces selects a particle treatment for a force-balance question and a rigid body for the slip angle — and the artifact records the caveat honestly that a particle treatment sufficing for one question is NOT evidence that the ladder is a particle, and cannot confirm full equilibrium. EQUATION-COUNT CONSEQUENCE, the sharpest teaching point: in the bracket case a particle model supplies two force equations in 2D and no moment equation, so the sought moment could not be obtained at all — the wrong model does not produce a wrong number, it produces no equation capable of answering the question. FIRST DRAFT BLOCKED on the Case 1 concurrency argument, a defect originating in Operator packet data rather than executor transcription. As drafted it claimed the three cable forces and the weight all act through the top attachment point, which is false of the weight — it acts at the centre of gravity — and it omitted the ball-and-socket base reaction from the force inventory entirely. In a skill whose subject is which forces act where, that is precisely the error the skill exists to prevent. Corrected under PHASE-D-PARTICLE-VS-RIGID-BODY-MODELING-CURSOR-CORRECTION-001 to state that concurrency is a property of LINES OF ACTION rather than points of application, to identify the weight's line of action as the vertical through the centre of gravity which is the mast axis and therefore passes through the top attachment point, and to inventory the base reaction with its axial direction derived from the stated premise that the three guy cables are symmetrically arranged and equally tensioned so their horizontal components cancel. All four force lines of action then meet at the top attachment point and the PARTICLE conclusion follows soundly. The correction improves the artifact beyond correctness: it now teaches that concurrency is tested on lines of action, a non-obvious point, where the original would have taught a student to check points of application — the wrong habit. A common_errors entry was added naming both failure modes. RECIPROCAL BOUNDARY, the central requirement of this lane: mechanics_model_selection owns the four-discriminator frame of equilibrium, size-and-shape, deformation and dimensionality, and raised the particle-versus-rigid-body question within its size-and-shape discriminator; this skill answers it. Verified that the four-discriminator frame is NOT re-authored and the complement is named in one sentence, so the two nodes compose without overlap. The signed FBD skills own diagram construction and none is drawn here; no equilibrium equation is written or solved; no numeric quantity is reported as a deliverable; no determinacy verdict; no deformation content, both particle and rigid body being rigid treatments. Equation counts are stated in prose as a consequence of the choice, which the scope requires, without any equation being written. One earned signal, unclassified at step 1, with the required cannot-be-earned analysis for all four others: axis_confusion no axis chosen or transformed; sign_or_placement_error no signed quantity or force placement authored; simple_average_used not a Centroids-family skill and no averaging step; solution_sequencing_error the criteria being independent with free order. Not padded. Honest limitation recorded: agreement of the three criteria confirms consistent application to the same reading of the situation but does not establish that the situation was read correctly — a misjudged concurrency would be applied consistently and all three criteria would still agree. SCHEMA-FIT FINDING, fourth conceptual data point: formula.notation carries a genuine decision rule with no invented algebra; formula.variables is EMPTY with symbol-free notation, following the precedent set by the signed sibling and consistent with the Architect ruling that conceptual skills carry a governing rule rather than an equation; worked_example.answer carries a classification label set rather than a computed result, real but strained; failure_signal_mappings honestly thin at one signal.

procedure_signature.notes: Virtual work — the principle of virtual work for equilibrium of a rigid one-degree-of-freedom system, the FINAL node of Phase D, authored to the Architect scope ruling for equilibrium analysis by compatible virtual displacement with deformation-energy and dynamics methods excluded. Independently re-derived: for a weightless bar of length L = 2 m pinned at O with a vertical load F = 100 N at the free end B and an applied couple M at the pin, the one-DOF coordinate theta gives y_B = L sin theta and the compatible virtual displacement delta y_B = L cos theta delta-theta, so delta U = M delta-theta - F L cos theta delta-theta = 0 yields M = F L cos theta = 100 x 2 x cos 30 = 173.21 N*m, and the direct-moment cross-check about O gives the identical 173.21 N*m by the other route. THE DROP-OUT IS THE ENTIRE POINT AND IS VISIBLE: the pin reaction at O does no virtual work because O is stationary under the compatible virtual displacement, so it never enters delta U = 0, and virtual work reaches the answer without the reaction appearing while the direct-equilibrium cross-check reaches the same number by a route that must reason about moments — the different route reaching the shared answer, one of them sidestepping the constraint force, being what makes virtual work its own method rather than a restatement of sum M = 0. The artifact never collapses it back into direct equilibrium: the cross-check is verification only, and re-deriving sum F = 0 / sum M = 0 as the primary route is flagged as a common error. The compatible virtual displacement is handled correctly, parameterized by one coordinate with positions differentiated to components and compatibility confirmed, and delta x_B = -L sin theta delta-theta is carried to note what a horizontal force would contribute without cluttering the vertical-load case. THE THREE-SIGNAL MAPPING is the most refined axis-versus-sign split in the corpus and is correct: axis_confusion at step 2 is pairing a force with the wrong virtual-displacement component, a vertical force with delta x_B instead of delta y_B, while sign_or_placement_error at step 3 is the wrong sign on a correctly paired term, the downward load taken as doing positive work when B rises; these are the two dominant virtual-work error modes, genuinely distinct acts at distinct steps with each trigger stating the distinction, and unclassified at step 1 carries the method-defeating boundary errors of including a non-working reaction in delta U, strain or kinetic energy, or an incompatible displacement. simple_average_used and solution_sequencing_error cannot be earned. THE SCOPE RULING HELD UNDER REAL TEMPTATION since virtual work is the gateway to energy and stability methods: the analysis stays rigid-body virtual work of applied forces only, with no strain energy, no kinetic energy, and no dynamics, and it names that delta U = 0 locates equilibrium while the stability second-derivative test is a separate question not authored, acknowledging the adjacent topic without entering it. The honest limitation is precise: virtual work gives the relation among active forces and not the constraint reactions, which need direct equilibrium if wanted, and it assumes frictionless constraints so reactions do no work, with friction they would contribute. The categorical-mismatch placement in GENERAL_PRINCIPLES among six meta-skills is handled by reading as the full method it is rather than meta-skilling itself to match neighbors, vindicating the FULL_HIBBELER_CORE tier. Symbol discipline: the virtual quantities delta-theta, delta U, delta x_B and delta y_B are introduced in distinct delta notation without rebinding any force or moment symbol as a virtual quantity, and M and theta reuse their applied-couple and angle meanings with M noted as found via delta U = 0 rather than sum M = 0. Eighth and final skill of Batch 4N; signed from its re-parented VIRTUAL_WORK location; required no correction at review; brings Phase D to 98 of 98 and completes the procedure authoring phase. Reviewed at full discipline with no relaxation for being the last node.
